_source: House style: edit here, both runtimes follow. v1.0.1: bare 'unlock' pulled from HARD phraseTells (strong functional sense, e.g. 'unlock this step/account/feature'; over-fired on progressive-disclosure UI microcopy in production, 2026-07-01); stays in watchlist for cluster-WARN. 'elevate'/'seamless' remain HARD (reliably filler as bare words). v1.0.2: added 'in today's <adj> world' (sibling of the fast-paced tell). Held as too functional/common for HARD (unlock precedent): 'a sense of / air of / notion of', 'here's the thing/kicker', bare 'worth noting/mentioning'; elevate/seamless demotion held pending a second consumer signal. v1.0.3: provenance note rewritten for release (internal sourcing references removed); tell definitions unchanged. v1.0.4 (2026-07-23, engine v1.0.6, dispatch 2026-07-23T163600Z-001 + 2026-07-23T171400Z-001): added a spaced/unspaced double-hyphen ('--') structural WARN in engine.js's findStructuralWarnings (NOT a catalog-driven charTells/phraseTells entry, since that group is hard-fail and a fleet blast-radius scan found ~41 already-shipped own-site pages using this em-dash-substitute construction; see engine.js's DOUBLE_HYPHEN_RE comment for the full reasoning). Promoted to hard ERROR on livingwebsites.ca's own served-page gate the same day, after the ~5 real own-site instances found were rewritten to real punctuation. Other tell definitions unchanged.
